summary: One independently testable behavior: verify the section 34 60 FPS target at 1080p in the browser during the largest encounter and each band's representative scene, using WI-07a's frame/FPS telemetry, and apply narrow fix-forward within the section 34 performance rules (particle pooling, AI culling far from player, ambient count caps, geometry/material reuse, instancing, no per-frame allocations in hot loops, small DOM footprint, moderate segment counts) only where a scene misses. The single changed subsystem is rendering and materials: all techniques operate in src/render/ (particle field, postfx, world/palette, spine renderer) and the per-frame visual work in src/game/Game.ts (renderVisuals, ambient scale), and the item explicitly excludes balance numbers (WI-07c) and scarcity/reachability (WI-07b). Boundaries are explicit: measure first, then apply the specific technique that closes the gap; no speculative pipeline rewrite; a stuttering large-creature reveal is a hard defect to fix; any gameplay-changing finding is routed to fix planning, not redesigned in place. Evidence is focused: recorded FPS / frame delta / active entity count per scene from WI-07a, before/after frame data for any applied fix, headless suite and build stay green, visual output unchanged. Criteria coverage: AC-bal-perf carried verbatim from ST-07, owned solely by WI-07d as named final proof owner. Dependency on WI-07a (the telemetry it reads) is correct; independence from WI-07c (balance tuning) and WI-07b (scarcity) is correctly stated. Handoff names specific files, sections, and the telemetry source, permitting a fresh implementer to proceed without reconstructing the project.
